# Exact three-fiber support gain and two admissible middle variations

This note concerns an actual convex family at the complete integer bases `{-1,0,1}`, with positive full-dimensional fibers `A,K,B` in `R^d`, `d>=1`, and `(A+B)/2 subset K`. It proves exact directional identities and actual normal-dependent convex potentials. No individual `Gamma_d` efficiency theorem, or low-depth counterexample, is claimed.

## 1. Circuit notation and the summed formal optimum

Let a regular positive critical circuit through `(0,y)` consist of caps

    H_j={a_j z+v_j.x>=b_j},  v_j!=0,
    b_j=v_j.y,  rho_j>0,  sum_j rho_j v_j=0.

Suppose every cap has common raw mass `Q`. Assume its full mixed section measure has centroid `(0,y)`, and its boundary has zero fiber-boundary measure. Proper, strictly empty and strictly full traces are allowed. Write

    sigma_jp=H_(d-1)(K_p intersect boundary H_j)/||v_j||,
    S_j=sum_p sigma_jp,
    theta_j=(rho_j/S_j)/(sum_l rho_l/S_l),
    C_p=sum_j theta_j |K_p intersect H_j|,
    T_p=sum_j theta_j sigma_jp v_j,
    B_p=sum_j theta_j sigma_jp (b_j-a_j p).

The regularity assumptions ensure `S_j>0`. The section's base-coordinate centroid gives `sigma_j,-=sigma_j,+=s_j`. Put

    T=T_-=T_+,
    M0=(A+B)/2,
    V=|A|+|K|+|B|.

The circuit weights give `sum_p T_p=0`, because `theta_j S_j` is one common positive multiple of `rho_j`. Consequently

    T_0=-2T.                                          (1)

Also `sum C_p=Q`. Finally

    sum_p B_p
      =sum_j theta_j [b_j S_j-a_j sum_p p sigma_jp]
      =y.sum_j theta_j S_j v_j=0.                     (2)

For each fiber define its **formal optimized numerator**

    F_p=d C_p+B_p+h_Kp(-T_p).                          (3)

This is the maximum, over actual `c_p in K_p`, of the integral of `W=sum theta_j 1_Hj` against the fiber radial boundary velocity `n.(x-c_p)`. The cap Gauss--Green identity is

    integral_(boundary K_p) W n.(x-c_p)
       =d C_p+B_p-T_p.c_p.                            (4)

At the two exposed endpoint bases, the values (3) are realized by the base-localized normal hinges proved in `candidate f5316a23a6622c7a`, Section 8. No such localization is asserted for the middle fiber.

Equations (1)--(3) give exactly

    F_-+F_0+F_+=dQ+2[h_M0(-T)+h_K(T)].                (5)

Here `h_A(-T)+h_B(-T)=2h_M0(-T)` and `h_K(2T)=2h_K(T)`. The summation uses both the circuit normalization and the actual base-section moment; dropping either invalidates the cancellation.

Set `G=h_M0(-T)+h_K(T)`. Midpoint inclusion implies

    G>=h_M0(-T)+h_M0(T)>=0.                            (6)

The right side is the width of the actual midpoint body in direction `T`. Since that body is full-dimensional, it is strictly positive if `T!=0`. This gives a strict *formal* gain in (5), not a quantitative `Gamma_d` bound. In particular dividing (5) by `dV` does not by itself produce an admissible globally convex potential realizing the independent three optimizers.

## 2. An actual center triangle realizes one hemisphere of that gain

Choose actual support minimizers

    p in argmin_A T.x,   q in argmin_B T.x,
    m=(p+q)/2,
    r in argmax_K T.x,
    D=r-m.

Compactness gives these points; midpoint inclusion gives `m in M0 subset K`. They satisfy

    T.D=G.                                            (7)

For each unit normal `n`, define on `-1<=z<=1`

    f(z)=m+z(q-p)/2,
    a_n(z)=n.f(z)+(1-|z|)(n.D)_+,
    Phi(n,z,x)=[n.x-a_n(z)]_+.                         (8)

The scalar function `a_n` is concave in `z`. Hence `Phi` is nonnegative and convex in the physical variables for each fixed normal, and is continuous in the normal. It is an admissible normal-bundle potential, with the same support-inequality erosion construction as the affine hinges.

The construction also has an actual geometric core: `a_n(z)` is the support function of the section at `z` of the triangle in ambient space with vertices `(-1,p),(0,r),(1,q)`. That triangle lies in the actual convex body. Its section is the segment joining `f(z)` to `f(z)+(1-|z|)D`. Thus `a_n(z)<=h_Kz(n)` for every real base, not only the three measured ones.

On the measured endpoint boundaries, (8) is the radial velocity about `p` or `q`. On the middle boundary it is

    n.(x-m)-(n.D)_+,                                 (9)

which is nonnegative because `max(n.m,n.r)<=h_K(n)`. The positive-part operation in (8) therefore makes no additional change on any measured boundary.

Let

    J=integral_(boundary K) (n.D)_+ dH_(d-1),
    L_+=integral_(boundary K) (n.D)_+ W dH_(d-1),
    L_-=integral_(boundary K) (-n.D)_+ W dH_(d-1).

The affine-center radial baseline `n.(x-f(z))` has total boundary integral `dV` and weighted integral `dQ`. To check the latter although `m` need not equal `y`, its summed cap correction is

    sum_j theta_j S_j v_j.(y-m)=0;

the base-coordinate corrections vanish by section centroids. Subtracting (9)'s explicit term proves

    integral Phi=dV-J,
    integral Phi W=dQ-L_+,
    efficiency(Phi)=(dQ-L_+)/(dV-J).                  (10)

The denominator is positive: the endpoint integrals are exactly `d(|A|+|B|)>0`, and the middle contribution is nonnegative. In particular there is no division by a vanishing formal quantity.

The constant-vector divergence theorem on middle caps gives

    integral_(boundary K) n W = T_0=-2T.

Pairing with `D` yields the exact split

    L_--L_+=2T.D=2G.                                 (11)

Thus (5)'s support gain is precisely the difference of the two weighted normal hemispheres in this construction. Only one hemisphere is subtracted by the admissible center triangle; asserting that the full independent middle optimizer is realized would lose this distinction.

For any prescribed `gamma`, this actual test pays `gamma` exactly when

    gamma J-L_+ >= d(gamma V-Q).                      (12)

Neither (6) nor (11) alone proves (12). The identity retains an explicit directional boundary quantity on the middle body, rather than replacing it by scalar volumes.

## 3. A different hinge isolates actual middle support slack

For unit `n`, set

    b_n(z)=[(1-z)h_A(n)+(1+z)h_B(n)]/2,
    Psi(n,z,x)=[n.x-b_n(z)]_+.                        (13)

The expression inside the positive part is affine in the physical variables for each fixed normal. On each endpoint normal bundle it is zero. On the middle boundary its value is exactly

    Delta(n)=h_K(n)-h_M0(n)>=0.                       (14)

Hence the exact denominator and numerator are

    integral Psi=d|K|-integral h_M0(n) dS_K(n),
    integral Psi W=integral_(boundary K) Delta(n) W dH_(d-1).  (15)

Here `dS_K` is the ordinary surface area measure, and `integral h_K dS_K=d|K|` is the divergence identity. Multiplication by a continuous nonnegative normal function is also admissible in the normal-bundle test class. Such tests localize (14) to actual directions of support slack. Their use requires a positive denominator.

That denominator can vanish even with **strict** midpoint inclusion. For an exact example in dimension two, take

    K={x,y>=0,x+y<=1},
    A=B=M0={x,y>=0,h<=x+y<=1},       0<h<1.

These are actual positive fibers of the convex hull at `-1,0,1`, and `M0` is a proper subset of `K`. Nevertheless `M0` touches all three supporting lines of `K`. Thus `h_M0=h_K` at each of the three normals carrying `dS_K`, so (13) vanishes on the entire measured normal bundle. A separate argument is needed whenever support slack vanishes `dS_K`-almost everywhere, not only when `K=M0`. No criticality is asserted for an arbitrary menu in this calibration.

## 4. Exact globally critical calibration with nonzero directional gain

Let `g=(1/3,1/3)`, take the same standard triangle `K` of area `1/2`, and set

    A=B=g+[-1/6,1/6] times [-1/12,1/12].

Their area is `1/18`, and they lie in `K` since their smallest coordinates are positive and their largest coordinate sum is `11/12<1`. The convex hull of the three lifted fibers therefore has exactly these fibers at its complete integer bases.

The three ambient caps, independent of `z`, are

    H1={x>=1/3}, H2={y>=1/3}, H3={x+y<=2/3}.         (16)

They are genuinely globally critical at `(0,g)`, with

    Q=2/9+1/18=5/18,      V=11/18.

For every nonvertical cap through `(0,g)`, the two endpoint contributions sum exactly to `|A|`: reflection about `g` pairs the opposite threshold shifts in the identical centrally symmetric endpoints. The middle triangle contributes at least `2/9` by its centroid inequality. Pure-integer caps contain the whole middle triangle. Conversely (16) cover the entire middle fiber and each has mass `Q`; endpoint planes can each be isolated by a cap of mass `1/18<Q`. This proves the claimed global depth against all ambient directions. All nine cuts are proper and their section centroids are `(0,g)` after summation.

The endpoint coarea lengths are `(1/6,1/3,1/6)`; the middle ones are `(2/3,2/3,2/3)`. Therefore

    theta=(4/11,3/11,4/11),
    T=(0,1/33),        T_0=(0,-2/33).

Choose `p=q=m=(1/3,1/4)` and `r=(0,1)`, so `D=(-1/3,3/4)`. Then

    G=1/44,
    F_-=F_+=23/396,    F_0=16/33,
    sum F_p=119/198=dQ+2G.                           (17)

On the three middle edges, the normalized profile means are respectively `16/33` on `y=0`, `14/33` on `x+y=1`, and `14/33` on `x=0`. Integration of the normal pairings gives

    J=3/4, L_+=7/22, L_-=4/11.

Hence the center-triangle potential (8) has exact efficiency

    (5/9-7/22)/(11/9-3/4)=94/187>4/9.               (18)

The endpoint-localized optimized efficiency is `23/44>4/9`. The middle-slack test (13), with normal multiplier supported near `-e_2`, has efficiency `16/33>4/9`; its support slack in that direction is `1/4`. All quantities are from the same actual critical configuration. Its depth `5/11` is above the OC threshold, so it is a calibration of the directional identities, not a low-depth family.

## 5. Scope of a conditional search

An actual globally critical example below `Gamma_2/2` in this complete three-fiber setting would already contradict OC. Accordingly that hypothesis is only used as a conditional inequality in a prospective proof. The identities above make no existence assertion for such a body. A counterexample to sufficiency of a smaller test class, if sought without that hypothesis, would have to be reported with its actual larger depth and would not refute OC.

The equal section weights and the actual midpoint support in (5), (11), and (15) come specifically from the complete equally spaced chain. Arbitrary unequally spaced sampled sites have different section moment weights and cannot be substituted here.

## 6. Endpoint coverage alone does not pay an individual circuit

Here is a separate ordinary-body obstruction, expressly **without** global criticality or a compatible three-fiber realization. It identifies why the shared hypotheses cannot be dropped from a future chain proof.

Let

    A=[-11/10,-9/10] times [-3,3],
    H1={x>=0}, H2={-x+y>=0}, H3={-x-y>=0},
    theta=(2/5,3/10,3/10), W=sum theta_j 1_Hj.

The three continuous normals form a positive circuit, and the caps cover the plane. In fact `H2,H3` already cover this entire rectangle. Nevertheless the supremum of

    integral_(boundary A) Phi(n,x) W / integral_(boundary A) Phi(n,x)

over all finite nonnegative normal-dependent potentials convex in the physical variable is exactly `41/100<4/9`.

On either horizontal edge `W=3/10`. On a vertical edge `x=-c`, where `c=9/10` or `11/10`, its profile is

    W(y)=3/10+(3/10)1_[-c,c](y).

For every nonnegative convex function `f` on `[-3,3]`,

    integral_[-c,c] f <= (c/3) integral_[-3,3] f.

Indeed the symmetrization `(f(t)+f(-t))/2` is nondecreasing for `t>=0`; its mean over `[0,c]` is no larger than its mean over `[0,3]`. Thus the efficiency on either vertical edge is at most `(3/10)(1+c/3)`, namely `39/100` on the right and `41/100` on the left. Adding the four nonnegative edge integrals gives the upper bound for every potential. A continuous normal multiplier supported near the left-edge normal, with constant physical value, attains `41/100` exactly.

This does not contradict the exposed-base theorem: the displayed caps are not asserted to be common global depth-attaining caps at a source in this rectangle. It rules out deriving individual `Gamma_2` efficiency merely from endpoint coverage and balanced positive continuous normals.
